# Raster

Namespace `Nfty.Model.Render` in assembly `Nfty.Model`.

```csharp
public static class Raster
```

The software rasterizer: transforms a [`Mesh`](Nfty.Model.Mesh.md) by a [`Camera`](Nfty.Model.Render.Camera.md)'s view-projection, clips against the near plane, culls back faces, resolves visibility with a z-buffer, samples the texture with nearest-neighbor filtering, and shades with flat, quantized, camera-relative lighting — the whole rendering pipeline the spec lists (see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-model-preview-design.md`, "Rendering"). Pure CPU pixel arithmetic: it renders identically headless and on screen, which is the entire reason this exists instead of a GPU control (\`Avalonia.Headless\` has no GL context).

## Remarks

Single-threaded by design: the z-buffer is shared state, so the pixel loop is not a `ParallelWork` candidate. Allocates nothing per call — the transformed vertices live in a pooled array and the texels are read in place (or from a pooled copy).

## Methods

### DrawEdges(Mesh, Camera, RenderTarget) { #m-drawedges-nfty-model-mesh-nfty-model-render-camera-nft-d1be29 }

```csharp
public static void DrawEdges(Mesh mesh, Camera camera, RenderTarget target);
```

Draws the outline of every visible quad over what [`Raster.Render()`](Nfty.Model.Render.Raster.md#m-render-nfty-model-mesh-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixl-d8d8ec) already put in `target`, one pixel wide: the wireframe display. A risen mesh is made of quads (four vertices, six indices each), so the outlines are the greedy faces' and walls' own edges, not the triangle diagonals. An outline is drawn only where it lies on the surface the z-buffer holds (a small relative tolerance), so edges behind the solid stay hidden, and it changes only a pixel's color, never its alpha or depth. The ink is white on a dark pixel and black on a light one, so it reads on any texture. A quad with a corner behind the near plane is skipped whole rather than clipped; the camera never enters the solid's box, so this only shows when zoomed to the surface.

**Parameters**

- `mesh` (`Mesh`) - The solid, already rendered into `target`.
- `camera` (`Camera`) - The camera that rendered it.
- `target` (`RenderTarget`) - The surface to draw on.

### Render(Mesh, Image&lt;Rgba32&gt;, Camera, RenderTarget) { #m-render-nfty-model-mesh-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixl-d8d8ec }

```csharp
public static int Render(Mesh mesh, Image<Rgba32> texture, Camera camera, RenderTarget target);
```

Draws every triangle of `mesh`, sampling `texture` nearest-neighbor, into `target`, as seen by `camera`. The projection is built here from `target`'s own size, so it can never disagree with the surface it is drawn on. Does not clear `target` first — the caller owns the background and calls [`RenderTarget.Clear()`](Nfty.Model.Render.RenderTarget.md#m-clear-sixlabors-imagesharp-pixelformats-rgba32) itself.

**Parameters**

- `mesh` (`Mesh`) - The mesh to draw.
- `texture` (`Image<Rgba32>`) - The face atlas the mesh was built against.
- `camera` (`Camera`) - The view to draw it from.
- `target` (`RenderTarget`) - The surface to draw into.

**Returns.** How many SOURCE triangles (index triples) survived clipping and culling and were rasterized; one split in two by the near plane counts once.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException` - `texture` is not the size of the art the mesh was risen from — the same rule `ModelWriter` applies.

### Render(Mesh, Image&lt;Rgba32&gt;, Camera, RenderTarget, PreviewLighting) { #m-render-nfty-model-mesh-sixlabors-imagesharp-image-sixl-11b55d }

```csharp
public static int Render(Mesh mesh, Image<Rgba32> texture, Camera camera, RenderTarget target, PreviewLighting lighting);
```

Draws the same clipped, nearest-neighbor preview as the original overload, with a preview-only light intensity and color. [`PreviewLighting.Default`](Nfty.Model.Render.PreviewLighting.md#p-default) preserves the original pixels. Texture alpha, depth, projection and exported model data are unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `mesh` (`Mesh`) - The mesh to draw.
- `texture` (`Image<Rgba32>`) - The face atlas the mesh was built against.
- `camera` (`Camera`) - The view to draw it from.
- `target` (`RenderTarget`) - The caller-cleared surface to draw into.
- `lighting` (`PreviewLighting`) - Preview light intensity and RGB color.

**Returns.** The number of source triangles surviving clipping and culling.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException` - The texture size disagrees with the mesh.
